newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND CONFIDENT OF REACHING FIRST EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND CONFIDENT OF REACHING FIRST EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund are confident of reaching their first European Cup final after a fortunate second-half goal from stand-in Rene Tretschok sealed a 1-0 victory over Manchester United in Wednesday's semifinal first leg.

Tretschok, a late replacement in a Dortmund team hit by a crop of injuries, hit a crisp shot from just outside the area in the 76th minute which took a cruel deflection off Gary Pallister into the top left-hand corner.
Goalkeeper Raimond Van der Gouw just got his fingers to the ball but was unable to stop it going into the top corner.
Although it was a lucky moment on a largely frustrating night for the German champions in their own Westfalen stadium, Dortmund deserved victory for their industry alone in difficult circumstances.

The Germans went into the game without a handful of first-choice players. In addition to suspended libero Matthias Sammer, they were missing key international strikers Karlheinz Riedle and Stephane Chapuisat and experienced defender Juergen Kohler.
Despite the problems they played the better football against a full-strength United team.

"It is a good result," coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "We are expecting a really intense atmosphere in the second leg in Manchester but we have an experienced team and go into the return leg feeling optimistic."
European footballer-of-the-year Sammer said: "We are in a good position after today and I hope we can go on like that. You have to show character in a difficult situation and we did well today."

Hitzfeld said he was surprised that United did not take the game to Dortmund more in the first half. But the English champions did have several good chances to score after the interval and were unlucky not to come away with a draw.

One of the biggest scares for the Germans came four minutes after the interval when midfielder Nicky Butt went desperately close to scoring. His fierce shot hit the left-hand post after a brilliant pass from the left from Frenchman Eric Cantona.

In the 66th minute another pass from Cantona put David Beckham clear on the right-hand side of the box. He struck the ball crisply towards goal but Dortmund defender Martin Kree managed to get his foot in the way at the last second.

"At the end of the day I think we underachieved," United manager Alex Ferguson said. "The disappointing thing is that we didn't manage to score away from home. Now we have to attack Dortmund at Old Trafford knowing that we can't afford to lose a goal."

United made a surprise late change just minutes before the kickoff, replacing Danish goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel, who has been suffering from a back injury, with Dutchman van der Gouw. He was thrown into a fast and furious game.
After all the pre-match worries about hooliganism the atmosphere in the packed Westfalen stadium, which boasted a capacity crowd of 48,500, was intense but good-humoured.
The furious pace of the game made the match look more like a domestic Cup tie than the tactical battles which are sometimes characteristic of matches at this stage of the competition.

Dortmund began confidently despite their problems. The speed of midfielders Andy Moeller and Paulo Sousa caused United problems in the middle and Joerg Heinrich was a constant threat down the left flank.
It was from a Heinrich cross that the Germans had their best chance of the first half in the 10th minute. Van der Gouw had to dive low to his right to stop a glancing header from Heiko Herrlich.
Herrlich, who has also just returned from injury, went close again with a close-range effort in the 28th minute but, with Van der Gouw well beaten, the ball trickled past the right-hand post.

United's only real chance in the first half came when Cantona fired a speculative long-range shot over the bar. But they started the second half with an extra bite and were quick to set up chances for Beckham and Butt.
